Understand Apache Spark’s Internal Working in Just 2 Minutes!


A must-know for every Data Engineer, especially if you're prepping for interviews or optimizing pipelines!

Ever triggered a Spark action like count() or collect() and wondered what actually happens behind the scenes? 🤔


This one visual breaks it all down — from driver execution to job cleanup — in just 11 crisp steps. Perfect for your quick daily learning dose! 

👇 Here's a high-level walkthrough:

1️⃣ Driver Program Begins Execution
Your Spark app kicks off with the driver initializing the Spark session and waiting for an action (like count()) to trigger the job.

2️⃣ Job is Submitted
The job and all dependencies are submitted to the Cluster Manager (YARN, Kubernetes, Standalone).

3️⃣ DAG Creation
The logical execution plan is transformed into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) — this maps all your transformations and actions.

4️⃣ Stage Breakdown: Narrow vs. Wide

Narrow: No data shuffling between partitions (e.g., map())

Wide: Triggers shuffle, requires data movement (e.g., groupByKey())


5️⃣ Tasks are Created
Each stage is broken into tasks — the smallest units of work, each tied to a data partition.

6️⃣ Application Master is Assigned
Cluster Manager spins up an Application Master to manage your job (in YARN, it's a container).

7️⃣ Code Sent to Executors
The driver sends serialized code and dependency info to worker nodes (executors).

8️⃣ Tasks Run on Worker Nodes
Tasks are executed in parallel across the cluster nodes based on their respective data partitions.

9️⃣ Shuffle Happens (if needed)
For wide stages, data is shuffled across executors → sorted → written to disk for downstream stages.

🔟 Driver Receives Results

For actions like collect(): results come back to driver memory.

For actions like save(): data is written to storage like HDFS, S3, etc.


1️⃣1️⃣ Job Cleanup
Spark shuts down executors, cleans up memory, and releases resources via the Cluster Manager.

🎯 Why this matters:
Knowing this flow helps you:

✓ Optimize job performance

✓ Write more efficient PySpark code

✓ Understand why shuffles slow things down

✓ Ace Spark-related interview questions
